promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: The knee pain on Sunday changes next week: we pull volume, swap the tempo for easy or cross-training, and keep the long run short and flat while you get the knee looked at.

flags.title: New right knee pain
flags.detail: sharp on downhills from mile 7, now aches going down stairs. New symptom, worth a professional look before more hard work.

flags.title: Long run cut short
flags.detail: planned 13 mi, stopped at 8.5 and walked home. Explains the low week; not a fitness problem.

flags.title: Tempo on Wednesday
flags.detail: holding it this week until the knee settles, not because the session was bad.

flags.title: Easy share still under 80 percent
flags.detail: 76 percent this week, pulled down by the tempo and the 35 percent in zone 3 on the long run.

flags.title: Shoe mileage
flags.detail: Ghost 16 at 149 mi, fine for now but start thinking about the next pair before 300.

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer: 1. I can't tell you what it is, and I won't try to; outside-of-knee pain that comes on at a set point in a run, bites on downhills and lingers on stairs is worth a visit to a sports physio this week rather than a guess from me. Please skip Wednesday's tempo. Hard running on a cranky knee is how a niggle becomes a layoff, and we have ten weeks, which is enough time to lose a week and still hit the start line fit. If the physio clears you to run easy, do that; if not, we cross-train and come back when it is quiet.

new.analysis:
Through Saturday the week was on plan: Tuesday 6, Wednesday tempo with clean 8:00/mi reps, Thursday 5, Saturday 4. Fitness is tracking: easy pace is 9:50 at 138 bpm, down from 9:53 at 139 a few weeks ago, and the Aug 9 long run held steady with only a 7 bpm drift.

What changed is the knee. Thursday showed a 2/10 tight note, Saturday a 1/10 before the run, then Sunday it turned sharp on downhills and you had to walk in. That is a pattern I take seriously, especially because you told me you have not had this before.

So next week is built around protecting it, not around training through it. The long run comes down to 8 mi, flat, easy effort, and you abort at the first sharp twinge rather than pushing to finish. Wednesday is easy or a bike or pool session instead of the tempo; if the knee is quiet by Thursday we are still on track, and if it is not we have not dug the hole deeper.

We have 10 weeks to the start line. One easy week now costs us almost nothing in marathon fitness; a forced three-week break in September would cost the goal. When the physio clears you, we rebuild the long run and put the tempo back in the following week.

settingsProposalBullets: Note the new right-knee symptom from Aug 13 – 16 (outside of knee, sharp on downhills, aches on stairs) in what I know about you, so we can track whether it resolves or recurs.
Add access to a bike or pool as a cross-training option, so I can plan around days when running is not sensible.

safetyCallouts.title: See a sports physio about the right knee.
safetyCallouts.body: New outside-of-knee pain that sharpened on downhills and now hurts going down stairs is worth a professional look this week before more hard running. I can't diagnose it. If it stays painful at rest, worsens day over day, swells, or you can't bear weight, bring that forward.

safetyCallouts.title: Stop a run if sharp knee pain returns.
safetyCallouts.body: Walk home, ice if that helps you, and tell me in your next check-in so we can adjust again.
